mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over a 6-month window raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25pp QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by >0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month stretches where UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in consumer savings (RSAFS) signals a tightening monetary stance combined with reduced household liquidity, which depresses consumption and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between housing starts (HOUST) and personal income (implied by PAYEMS) over two consecutive quarters signals robust residential demand and construction activity, which boosts materials and financial sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS both rise QoQ for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and PAYEMS rise QoQ for two straight quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA for two straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals broad-based demand expansion, which elevates earnings expectations and yields positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during high-inflation episodes (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO above 12-month MA for 3 months AND CPIAUCSL <= 3% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and INDPRO are above their 12-month MAs for three months and CPIAUCSL <= 3% YoY.
